title: Canary backfill decision briefing
content:
Meeting: Rapid decision sync — canary backfill options
Date: 2026-03-10 09:30 PT
Attendees: Lina Moreno (owner), Tom Wu (release lead), Evan Brooks (SRE), Priya Desai (runtime eng), Marta Kline (customer ops), slack observers: #release-ops
Location: Zoom + #release-ops thread

Purpose / tl;dr:
We observed a small but reproducible regression in the hosted API for long context chat sessions (95th p99 latency spike) affecting ~2.1% of requests after yesterday's canary. This doc captures the decision options discussed in the 30-minute sync and records the chosen path: targeted backfill patch rollout to canary+10% then progressive ramp to 50% with throttled burst capacity and close SLO watch, unless immediate customer impact forces rollback. Action owners and short-term mitigations below.

Background & what we know:
- Canary deployed on 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC (REL-2123). Baseline canary cohort < 1% of traffic initially.
- Regression: p95 and p99 token generation latency increased for sequences > 4096 tokens. Median unaffected.
- Root cause candidate: interaction between new prefix-caching heuristics and batching heuristic when KV cache miss occurs for large sequences (runtime change from PR #1864).
- Incidents flagged: two enterprise customers reported degraded UX; no data exfiltration/security issue.
- SRE notes: CPU and memory profiles spike correlated with cache misses; node-level OOMs not seen; autoscaler responded but came with increased scheduling latency.

Observed impact metrics (summary):
- p50 latency: +2% (negligible)
- p95 latency: +28% overall for affected route model-4k-longseq
- p99 latency: +85% on affected cohort
- Error rate: steady (no increase in 5xx)
- Affected traffic share: 2.1% (long context >=4096 tokens)

Decision options discussed:
1) Full rollback of REL-2123 to previous runtime commit. Pros: fastest return to known-good. Cons: loses other optimizations (smaller cost improvements), rollback window will touch all regions, will impact scheduled Dedicated deployments relying on new kernel selection. Requires change window (30–45 mins).

2) Targeted backfill patch (recommended). Create a small runtime patch that:
   - toggles off new prefix-cache heuristic for sequences >= 4096 OR
   - forces single-request-path (no batching) for those sequences to avoid KV miss interplay.
   Pros: surgical, preserves most benefits, smaller blast radius. Cons: patch needs quick QA, possible edge-case regressions untested.

3) Canary widening + playbook mitigations. Keep canary commit but widen to 10% immediate + 50% over 4 hours while throttling problematic route via routing rule and enabling conservative batching. Pros: low development churn. Cons: widens exposure; if regression scales, could increase customer impact.

4) Wait-and-observe with customer-tier throttling. No code changes today; add temporary per-customer QoS (rate-limit long contexts) and monitor for 24 hours. Pros: minimal release churn. Cons: customers degrade, poor CX, longer investigation window.

Context from teams:
- Runtime (Priya): Patch implementing a per-sequence heuristic flip is straightforward (~8–12h dev+50m canary QA), low code churn.
- SRE (Evan): Prefer quick rollback if impact increases; temporary routing rule can limit exposure to top 10 enterprise customers in minutes.
- Customer Ops (Marta): Top two reporting customers are in flight: customer A has active demo this afternoon; customer B is non-critical. Customer A prefers rollback vs degraded demo.

Decision reached (consensus):
- Proceed with option 2: surgical backfill patch that disables the new prefix-caching optimization for sequences >= 4096.
- Cut the patch branch now (Lina), dev task assigned to Priya for implementation, target for code ready to test in 8–10 hours.
- Quick QA plan: unit + smoke + controlled canary (canary cohort expanded to 10%) for 30 mins, then ramp to 50% over 2 hours if stable.
- If canary shows any p99 regression > +20% relative to baseline, immediate rollback to previous commit will be the trigger.

Short-term mitigation (while patch in flight):
- SRE to add per-route throttling rule for model-4k-longseq to cap long-context concurrency at current baseline levels (Evan, ETA 30m). Implement via routing policy to spare top demo customers if possible.
- Feature-flag audit: ensure we can toggle prefix-caching heuristic remotely (Priya to validate flag gating in prod).
- Customer Ops to proactively message Customer A with rollback plan and ETA (Marta).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Lina: create backfill branch & PR skeleton, post to #release-ops, assign reviewers (due 2026-03-10 EOD).
- Priya: implement heuristic toggle and smoke tests; attach perf benchmark results to PR (due 2026-03-11 06:00 UTC).
- Evan: deploy routing cap for model-4k-longseq and add grafana alert for p99 delta > +15% (due immediate, 2026-03-10 10:00 PT).
- Tom: prepare rollback playbook update (step-by-step, contact list, change window approx 30–45m) and be on-call during patch rollout (due 2026-03-10 12:00 PT).
- Marta: customer comms drafts for Customer A (rollback/backfill options) and coordinate demo alternatives (due 2026-03-10 11:00 PT).
- QA: run synthetic long-context load on canary nodes, baseline vs patched, upload raw traces to REL-2123 ticket (owner: QA rotation, due 2026-03-11 08:00 UTC).

Risk register (quick):
- Regressions in edge sequences where caching provides correctness (unlikely but verify with GRF tests).
- Patch introduces perf oscillation at high concurrency; mitigated by controlled canary and throttles.
- Rollback procedural risk: some regions have ongoing Dedicated deploys scheduled; coordinate with Infra (Tom) to avoid collision.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Does the new kernel selection path have telemetry gaps for long sequences? (Priya to add a small tracer instrument to PR)
- Can we implement a transparent path that uses last-known-good caching behavior for enterprise customers only? (future item — assign to product infra for feasibility study)
- Need long-term fix plan: decide whether we keep new heuristic with more robust KV miss handling or revert permanently. (postmortem item in REL-2123)

Meeting notes / conversational fragments (raw):
- Marta: "Customer A has an investor demo at 3pm; rolling back is their preference unless we can guarantee a fix before then."
- Evan: "I can put a routing cap in place now — buys time."
- Priya: "Patch is small; main risk is untested interaction paths. We'll smoke test against synthetic traces we have for long sessions."

Post-meeting timeline (planned):
- 09:30 meeting: decision to backfill (this doc).
- 09:45: Evan deploys routing cap.
- 10:00: Lina opens backfill PR skeleton.
- 18:00: Priya's patch ready for internal canary QA.
- 19:00: Controlled canary (10%) start; monitoring window 30m.
- If stable, ramp 10% -> 50% 19:30–21:30.

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- Keep communication tight to #release-ops and use the "canary-backfill" tag in PRs.
- Ensure rollback runbook has explicit region order and PostgreSQL migration check (even though none expected).
- Postmortem: schedule follow-up blameless postmortem for REL-2123 in 72 hours after stable resolution.

Linked tickets and references:
- REL-2123: Canary runtime change (PR #1864) — includes perf artifacts
- HOT-409: Customer A helpdesk thread (demo impact)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1864
- Confluence page: Release Playbook - Canary Procedures (see rollback appendix)

Appendix (quick checklist for rollout owner):
- [ ] Verify feature-flag state can be toggled remotely for prefix-cache.
- [ ] Confirm QA synthetic traces represent >=4096 token sessions.
- [ ] Update Grafana dashboard with canary cohort tag.
- [ ] Prepare short customer-facing FAQ for 15m status updates.

End of notes.

Document history: created 2026-03-10 by Lina Moreno in response to REL-2123 canary regression. Last modified 2026-03-12 to add QA dates and small timeline adjustments.
